title: Warren Buffett at UGA 2001: choose character, stay in your circle of competence, buy wonderful businesses
summary: Buffett answers University of Georgia students on character and habits, circle of competence, intrinsic value as discounted cash, the cigar-butt mistake, mistakes of omission, market temperament, philanthropy, and why small businesses can beat scale.

principles.text: Hire for intelligence, energy and integrity; without integrity, you want them lazy and dumb.
principles.quote: we look for three things when we hire people we look for intelligence we look for for initiative or energy and we look for integrity

principles.text: Invest only in what you understand; knowing the edge of your circle of competence matters more than its size.
principles.quote: defining your circle of competence is the most important aspect of investing it's not how important how large your circle is

principles.text: A big industry does not mean profits for investors; autos, airlines and TVs destroyed capital despite transforming society.
principles.quote: understanding the economic characteristics of a business is different than predicting the fact that an industry is going to do wonderfully

principles.text: Intrinsic value is the discounted cash a business will give you over its life; investing is laying out money now to get more later.
principles.quote: the only reason for making an investment and laying out money now is to get more money later on right that's that's what investing is all about

principles.text: Prefer a wonderful business at a fair price to a fair business at a wonderful price; time favors great businesses.
principles.quote: I would rather buy a wonderful business at a fair price than a fair business at a wonderful price

principles.text: Temperament beats brains: detaching from the crowd is what makes you rich.
principles.quote: it doesn't take brains it takes temperament it takes the ability to sit there and look at something
